rationale: This sample is dominated by floating-point tight-loop kernels (flops 1-8, whetstone, fbench, ffbench, himenobmtxpa, oourafft) where every transformed instruction executes millions of times, so the table weights passes by their loop-body overhead: SUB is nearly free and semantically safe, so it gets strong SecurityGain/DiversityGain with minimal cost weights and can apply broadly to raise per-instruction analysis difficulty; SPLIT is likewise cheap and mainly boosts diversity/size without hurting hot paths; BCF and FLA are kept applicable only with high RuntimeCost (0.8/0.9) and SizeCost sensitivity so the selector steers them toward cold, control-flow-rich code (the richards scheduler, schedule/worker dispatch, main) rather than the numeric kernels; IBR's indirect branches and ICALL's indirect calls break branch-predictor and BTB efficiency in tight loops, so both carry elevated RuntimeCost weights while still contributing on the call/branch-dense richards core (workfn, handlerfn, schedule); IGV gets moderate weights to hide global state access patterns without multiplying loads in the FP kernels. CorrectnessRisk weights stay low overall because all seven passes preserve semantics, but FLA/IBR carry the highest since flattening and indirect branching interact worst with floating-point exception-sensitive and self-timing code (ffbench, fbench).
